children: Harish Kumar Dhingra takes charge from 18 September following Sanjay Bhandari’s resignation on health grounds

Uttam Sugar Mills has appointed Harish Kumar Dhingra as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), effective 18 September, following the resignation of Sanjay Bhandari, who held the position for nearly two decades. Dhingra, an internal finance executive who has been with the company since 2005, moves into the role at a time when the sugar producer is facing near-term pressure on profitability.

Dhingra was serving as General Manager – Finance before his elevation to CFO. He brings more than three decades of experience in finance and corporate operations and has spent over 20 years with Uttam Sugar Mills.
He joined the company in 2005 as Assistant Manager and was elevated to General Manager – Finance in July 2017. His experience covers financial accounting, management and corporate operations.
The appointment provides continuity within the finance function following Bhandari’s departure.
Bhandari resigned from the CFO position citing health and medical reasons. He was relieved of his responsibilities on 16 September, bringing an end to a tenure of nearly 20 years in the role.
The company appointed Dhingra as his successor within two days of Bhandari’s exit. The transition also coincides with Uttam Sugar Mills’ 31st Annual General Meeting held on 18 September.
The change in finance leadership comes as the company manages the cyclical nature of the sugar business alongside its distillery and power operations.

Uttam Sugar Mills reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 2,209.92 crore in FY26, marking a 19.19 per cent year-on-year increase. Consolidated net profit rose 17.24 per cent to Rs 100.59 crore during the year.

The company, however, reported a sharp decline in profitability during Q1 FY27. Consolidated net profit fell 91.05 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.30 crore, reflecting pressure on margins during the quarter.
The new CFO therefore takes charge against a backdrop of weaker near-term profitability and the seasonal dynamics of the sugar industry.

Dhingra’s immediate responsibilities will include overseeing the company’s financial function as it enters the next sugarcane crushing cycle. Working capital management, capital allocation and financial planning will remain important as the company balances its sugar operations with its distillery and ethanol-related activities.
His elevation also keeps the finance leadership within the existing management structure, with an executive familiar with the company’s operations taking over after Bhandari’s long tenure.

The CFO transition comes at an important point in the company’s operating cycle, with the performance of the upcoming crushing season and movement in input costs likely to remain relevant to its financial performance.
